It appears in horror and science-fiction film scores, including Universal's genre pictures, the ethereal music James Bernard wrote for Hammer's "The Gorgon", several scores by Jerry Goldsmith, and the entr'acte music of "Gone with the Wind"; it is also heard on recordings such as Vera Lynn's song accompaniments and Slim Gaillard's "Novachord Boogie".

The Novachord is the world's first commercial polyphonic synthesiser, an electrophone keyboard instrument designed by John M. Hanert, Laurens Hammond and C. N. Williams and built by the Hammond company. It uses vacuum-tube monostable circuits as frequency dividers, deriving 72-note polyphony from twelve top-octave oscillators, and it has envelope, filter and tremolo controls. Playing it does not follow traditional piano or organ technique, and the panel parameters have to be adjusted frequently. At the 1939 New York World's Fair the Ford stand was played daily by Ferde Grofé's Novachord Orchestra, with four Novachords and a Hammond organ, and the instrument was later much used in science-fiction and horror film scores and in the studio.
諾瓦科德電子琴由約翰·M·哈納特、勞倫斯·哈蒙德與C·N·威廉斯設計，哈蒙德公司: The Novachord was designed by John M. Hanert, Laurens Hammond and C. N. Williams and built by the Hammond company, and it is regarded as the world's first commercial polyphonic synthesiser. Production began in November 1938, and it was first played in public at the 1939 New York World's Fair; on 30 January 1940 the first instrument was delivered to President Franklin D. Roosevelt. Because of parts shortages and poor sales, production stopped in 1942, with only 1,069 built, and it was never made again after the war. Its timbres were later much used in science-fiction and horror film and television scores, and it appears on recordings from the 1939 to the 1950s.
諾瓦科德電子琴音色具有獨特的電子質感，兼具溫潤與明亮的特徵。其音色範圍寬廣，涵蓋: The Novachord's timbre has a distinctive electronic quality that is both warm and bright. Its range is wide and covers the bass, middle and treble registers, and it can produce anything from a warm string-like texture to a clear synthetic tone. It uses subtractive synthesis, and filtering and envelope shaping give the timbre many layers and plenty of dynamic variation. It resonates through the interaction of electronic oscillators, which gives the tone its own character. Compared with a traditional organ, the Novachord sounds more modern and more flexible; compared with classical instruments, it has more of an electronic quality and a wider range. Its polyphony lets it sound several notes at once, which opened new possibilities for early electronic music and made it an important milestone in music history.
